reviews.text: This app is very promising. It isn't perfect, though. It still needs to be more accurate in its evaluations. For instance, it often misses initial consonant sounds that you have actually pronounced and, most importantly, it doesn't recognize the changes of sounds that normally occur in natural connected speech. For instance, when you're asked to say "nice to meet you" you need to pronounce the "t" in "meet" and the "j" sound in "you" very carefully. If you don't and you link both sounds and make a "ch" sound--which is what most native speakers do when they speak casually--ELSA points that out as a mistake. Once these details are corrected, ELSA will become a great app for learners of English as a foreign or second language.

ELSA Speak has a serious design flaw that undermines its inclusivity. During registration, users are required to select a “native language,” yet the list is extremely limited and excludes many legitimate languages. There is no option for “Other” or free input, forcing users to either misrepresent themselves or abandon the app. For a platform that claims to support global English learners, this is both short-sighted and exclusionary. Language diversity is not optional—it’s fundamental.

reviews.text: Very useful and user friendly app. I would recommend it to every English learner as it providess a unique way to train pronunciation, reading and speaking skills. Their AI-based pronunciation recognition system is amazing. It provides users with immediate results and highlights all possible mistakes. I would like share an idea for improvement the dialogue-based lessons. It would be great to see the results of the previous recording of a long sentence while making a new one.

I haven't used this app or anything, but the ad was extremely inaccurate. It claims to use IPA to teach you the correct accent, but the ad showed otherwise. I live in Britain, the app may have been aiming for another accent, but the wrong vowels were shown in the ad than what they are supposed to be. In addition, the IPA shown in the ad completely omitted long vowels (Eg "bath" is pronounced /'ba:θ/, not /baθ/). Also there was inaccurate liason. "meet you" is pronounced "meechyoo", not "mi tyoo"
